metadata.time_note: Storm Data entry times should be reviewed in local Standard Time (ST), not daylight time. Candidate reports include standard_time_display.
metadata.tornado_track_policy: Tornado tracks must come from DAT. NCEI begin/end coordinates are not used as a tornado track substitute.

properties.event_narrative: Rocky Mountain Power reported a power pole snapped by high winds and wires down near Cedar City.

Flash flooding in the Forsyth Burn Scar was reported by the Emergency Manager saying portions of the town of Pine Valley were cut off due to high water over roads_ and the Santa Clara River ran out of its banks.
Zion National Park Ranger reported flooding issues happening in the park with a group of 50 hikers unable to cross a trail due to flooding.
Video showing water and small rocks flowing over the SR190 in Big Cottonwood that led to law enforcement needing to close the mouth of the canyon temporarily.
Gauge on Paria River at Highway 89 increased from 300 CFS to 2225 CFS.
Spotter reported a large amount of pea-sized hail_ followed by a short-lived burst of penny sized hail on the backside. Time is approximate.
A Zion National Park employee reported muddy flowing water across SR 9 in Springdale near the entrance to Zion National Park.
Zion National Park reported flash flooding in Behunin Canyon and upper Emerald Pools with hikers stranded.
Snow Canyon State Park reported a road and trail closure about a mile and half in from the south entrance of the park due to flash flooding.
Corrects previous flash flood report from 8 ESE Bloomington. USGS gauge FPWU1 along Fort Pearce Wash observed a peak flood wave of 1890 cfs.
USGS gauge FPWU1 along Fort Pearce Wash observed a peak flood wave of 1890 cfs.
USGS gauge at Fort Pierce Wash showed ongoing flash flood wave that started around 4PM with a peak flow of 1890 cfs.
USGS gauge ESCU1 along the Escalante River observed a maxiumum flood wave of 767 cfs.
Trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail via social media.
At 704 PM MDT_ Zion National Park rangers reported flash flooding ongoing across the park. The USGS gauge located on the North Fork of the Virgin River has also observed a rise of around 3 feet.
House Rock Valley Road to Wire Pass washed out due to flooding. Estimated to have occurred some time Wednesday night_ exact time not known.
USGS gauge PAKU1 along the Paria River reported a maximum flood wave of 2448 cfs.
USGS gauge SRSU1 along the Santa Clara River observed a peak flood wave of 203 cfs.
Backcountry guide reported high flows and flooding on Wahweap Creek.
Washington County Water Conservancy reported large flows into the Virgin River originated from North Creek_ with flooding and impacts to residences along Kolob Terrace Road.
UDOT reported a closure of SR 59 due to flooding and debris. The road is closed EB at MP 18 and WB at MP 15.
USGS river gauge Virgin River at Virgin rose sharply from 400 cfs to 4290 CFS (with over a 2000 cfs rise in just 15 minutes).
Urban and small stream flooding resulting in some muddy water over streets resulting in cleanup by road crews.
Ongoing flash flooding along Gould Wash. Hurricane Police issued evacuation orders for residences immediately along Gould Wash which is running out of its banks through Hurricane.
USGS gauge on the Fremont River near Cainville showed high flows up to 1120 CFS.
Video of high flows on the Escalante River near Birch Creek merger.
USGS gauge on the Escalante river remains elevated_ has set a new event peak of 1660 CFS as of 1025 AM MDT.

Capitol Reef National Park reported high flows on the Fremont River_ with a road closure on SR-24 between mile markers 80 and 86. In addition Scenic Drive is closed_ Sulfur Creek is running near bank full_ and numerous waterfalls are observed. Described as gradual flooding over time_ not the typical flash flooding seen in the park.
Escalante River flooding muddy water over the 300 E bridge just north of the town of Escalante.
Flood waters and debris over New Harmony Road (old highway 144) and water impacting some homes near New Harmony.
Escalante River continues to flood across the flood plain near the Calf Creek inlet.
A rise of about 2 feet occurred on the North Fork of the Virgin River.
East bound lane of state route 29 is washed out near mile marker 9 below Joe's Valley reservoir. EM believes it occurred just after midnight.
FREUT UUNET site.

The Paria River experienced 3 main flood waves_ the first to around 2400 CFS by 730 PM Oct 21_ the next to 2700 CFS by about 4 PM on Oct 22_ and the last and largest was to 3150 CFS around 355 AM Oct 23.
